@graph.name: Ports & Intermodal Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The master dataset of the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the six ports the company's crews serve with logistics project management, specialized labor, ocean container packing and unpacking, loading and unloading, cross-docking, transloading, 3PL support and freight rework — the Virginia Inland Port at Front Royal, the Port of Virginia at Norfolk (Norfolk International Terminals, Virginia International Gateway, Portsmouth Marine Terminal and Newport News Marine Terminal), Richmond Marine Terminal, the Port of Baltimore, the Port of Wilmington, Delaware, and PhilaPort at Philadelphia. Each port is a full entity: authority and operator of record, terminal facts with acreage, berths, depth and capacity where the port authority publishes them, cargo specialties, rail service with on-dock and interchange qualifiers, highway corridors, foreign-trade-zone facts where designated, labeled volume figures with their sources and periods, current status items, and the branch binding that assigns the port to Winchester, VA or Martinsburg, WV by verified road distance. Portsmouth Marine Terminal is recorded as what it is — a heavy-lift and offshore-wind hub, not a container terminal; Virginia International Gateway is recorded as leased, not port-authority-owned; the Port of Wilmington's operator of record is Enstructure. No volume figure is published for the Virginia Inland Port, Richmond Marine Terminal or the Port of Wilmington, because none is verified. The company's crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards. The offer set does not include drayage: the company does not run port drayage — freight moves on the customer's or carrier's trucks, and the company's crews do the hands-on work at port-adjacent warehouses, receivers' docks, yards, leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes. Every fact carries its source; the companion coverage-matrix node in this file maps all 48 port-by-service cells.
@graph.keywords: ports, intermodal, transloading, container labor, devanning, cross-docking, freight rework, 3PL support, logistics project management, Virginia Inland Port, Port of Virginia, Norfolk, Richmond Marine Terminal, Port of Baltimore, Port of Wilmington, PhilaPort, TWIC card, branch binding

@graph.name: Ports Service Coverage Matrix Dataset
@graph.description: The service-coverage matrix of the Ports & Intermodal program: 48 cells — six ports by the eight attached services (transloading; ocean container packing and unpacking; loading and unloading / container labor; cross-docking; freight rework; specialized workforce; logistics project management; 3PL support services) — each cell recording whether the service is offered at the port, the treatment the program gives it (S, a dedicated spoke page; H, a hub section; D, dataset and hub mention only, the deliberate treatment for the secondary nodes), the delivery points where the work is performed, and the bound branch. Delivery points come from one enum only: port-adjacent warehouse, receiver's dock, yard, leased space, and on-terminal by arrangement — on-terminal work happens only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes, never as a bare claim. Every cell binds to its port's branch: Winchester, VA for the Virginia Inland Port, the Port of Virginia and Richmond Marine Terminal; Martinsburg, WV for Baltimore, Wilmington and PhilaPort (PhilaPort on drive time — road miles are tied).

@graph.name: Virginia Inland Port
@graph.description: Virginia Inland Port (Front Royal, VA) — inland intermodal terminal (dry port). Authority: Virginia Port Authority. Operator: Virginia Port Authority. Cargo: intermodal containers moving between rail and truck under steamship bill of lading; on-site log stuffing. Rail: Norfolk Southern — on-terminal intermodal rail; the terminal sits adjacent to the NS Crescent Corridor main line; rail is the long-haul leg to and from the Norfolk Harbor terminals (NIT, VIG), truck is the last-mile leg. Highway corridors: I-81, I-66. Foreign-trade zone: FTZ 20, Site 7 — Warren County Industrial Corridor (490 acres, Routes 340/522/661) (grantee Virginia Port Authority). U.S. Customs port of entry. Branch binding: this port is served from the Winchester, VA branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 23 road miles from Winchester and 43 from Martinsburg; bound to Winchester on miles. about 20 mi / about 20 min closer from Winchester.

@graph.name: Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore
@graph.description: Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore (Baltimore, MD) — deepwater marine port (containers, RoRo, autos, forest products, breakbulk). Authority: Maryland Port Administration (MDOT MPA). Operator: Maryland Port Administration (public terminals are state-owned and MPA-managed; Seagirt is operated by Ports America Chesapeake under a 50-year public-private partnership from 2010). Cargo: containers (Seagirt); RoRo farm and construction equipment — highest tonnage of any U.S. port (887,513 tons, 2025); forest products — first among U.S. ports (1.1M tons, 2025); autos and light trucks — second in the U.S. (728,225 units, 2025). Rail: CSX — on-dock at the ICTF adjacent to Seagirt (CSX Intermodal); CSX direct to all North Locust Point berths; Norfolk Southern — serves the port via interchange / Canton Railroad — not an on-dock Seagirt operator. Highway corridors: I-95, I-695, I-70, I-83, I-81. Volume (CY2025, calendar): 1,113,309 TEU — Port of Baltimore containers — a port record (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 887,513 short tons — RoRo farm and construction equipment — highest of any U.S. port (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 1,100,000 short tons — Forest products — first among U.S. ports (published as 1.1M tons) (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 728,225 units — Autos and light trucks — second in the U.S. (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Branch binding: this port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 106-116 road miles from Winchester and 91-96 from Martinsburg; bound to Martinsburg on miles. modest margin, about 12-18 mi; Winchester is a credible support branch.

@graph.name: Port of Wilmington
@graph.description: Port of Wilmington (Wilmington, DE) — deepwater marine port (fruit, reefer, breakbulk, RoRo). Authority: Diamond State Port Corporation (State of Delaware). Operator: Enstructure (operator since 31 July 2023 under a long-term concession; the former GT USA Wilmington / Gulftainer concession was cancelled). Cargo: fresh fruit, bananas and juice concentrate (verified claim form only: North America's top port for imports of fresh fruit, bananas and juice concentrate); refrigerated cargo; breakbulk and project cargo; autos (RoRo). Rail: Norfolk Southern — direct access per operator material; CSX — serves the Wilmington area via Wilsmere Yard; on-dock status unverified. Highway corridors: I-495, I-95, I-295. Branch binding: this port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 165 road miles from Winchester and 150 from Martinsburg; bound to Martinsburg on miles. about 16 mi closer from Martinsburg; drive time near-tied.

@graph.name: PhilaPort — Port of Philadelphia
@graph.description: PhilaPort — Port of Philadelphia (Philadelphia, PA) — deepwater marine port (containers, reefer, breakbulk, forest products, autos). Authority: PhilaPort (Philadelphia Regional Port Authority, Commonwealth of Pennsylvania). Operator: Private terminal operators under lease (landlord port): Packer Avenue — Greenwich Terminals LLC; Tioga — Delaware River Stevedores; Southport Auto — Glovis America. Cargo: refrigerated and perishable cargo — 64 percent of containerized imports were refrigerated (CY2025); containers; forest products (newsprint, coated paper, wood pulp); breakbulk and project cargo; cocoa (Pier 84); autos. Rail: CSX — at every PhilaPort terminal, via Conrail Shared Assets switching; Norfolk Southern — at every PhilaPort terminal, via Conrail Shared Assets switching. Highway corridors: I-95, I-76, I-70, I-81. Volume (CY2025, calendar): 889,268 TEU — PhilaPort containers — a port record (+6 percent; +39 percent since 2020) (source: The Produce News / PhilaPort, CY2025 results, via ports program dossier §1.5). Branch binding: this port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 193 road miles from Winchester and 191 from Martinsburg; bound to Martinsburg on time. bound on drive time only — road miles are tied (difference 0-3 mi); no mileage advantage is claimed.
